title: Riemann Hypothesis over Finite Holographic Substrate

blocks.title: Inputs and foundations: imported, declared, or proved

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The framed substrate: the Carrier's chart $\F_\Omega$, $\Omega=4\dS+1$, the Subject $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$, $\p=4\kp+1$, with $\pi=2\kp$, $\im=\gen^{-\kp}$, $\E=\gen^{\,\im}$; the four cardinal domains, labelled in the Carrier register and read by the Subject as counts; the orbital sphere with its latitudes; the shell Fourier transform on the phase cycle; time as the drive.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Finitude: for any reading of capacity $R$ the registered Universe embeds in the shell of $R$ members, and among $R+1$ members two share a residue; the totality is finite, its cardinality $\Omega$.
rows.name: finitude

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: Completeness: whatever exists is registered within, the registration of any totality being onto its registered Universe, so there is no outside and no host; two shells each registered whole within the other have one count.
rows.name: completeness_of_totality

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: Observation: every observation is a registration by an embedded part of $o<\Omega$ states; every reading identifies two members, and a complete reading needs the whole count; one translation carries each member to each.
rows.name: incompleteness_of_observation

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The Carrier: a timeless torsor of $\Omega$ elements, its cardinality its only absolute characteristic; reframings $x\mapsto ax+b$ are automorphisms, so $0$, $1$, $-1$ are frame data; a Subject's frame charts it as the prime field $\F_\Omega$, never the Carrier. Its capacity $\dS$ is the horizon entropy, $\Omega=4\dS+1$, and a Subject is embedded under $\p^{2}<\Omega$.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: The classical apparatus, as the chart of the shell: the explicit formula $\psi(x)=x-\sum_\rho x^{\rho}/\rho-\dots$; the line $\Real s=\half$, the pole at $1$ and the symmetry $s\mapsto1-s$; the dilation generator $-i(x\partial_x+\tfrac12)$ of Berry--Keating; the first eighty heights of the zeros of $\zeta$; Riemann's formula for the count $\pi(x)$ of the primes and Perron's formula; the Riemann spectrum of the primes.

rows.label: A8
rows.predicate: The chart's known off-line case: the Davenport--Heilbronn series, a Dirichlet series with a functional equation under $s\mapsto1-s$ and no Euler product, has zeros off the line, the first pair $s=0.8085171825+85.6993484854\,i$ and $1-\bar s$.

blocks.title: The shell: the frames, the primes, the zeta of the shell

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The two frames and their alignment: the Carrier's chart $\F_\Omega$, held by no embedded observer, and the Subject $\Fp$, $\p^{2}<\Omega$. Shared: the origin, the unit and the rules of arithmetic, so the labels of the window and the counts of the modes. Not shared: the generator and the drive; the cycles admit no projection ($12\nmid232$).
rows.name: two_frames_alignment

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: Frame coincidence within the observational horizon $\q$, the largest label with $\q^{2}<\p$: for $n\le\q$ the residue $n$ is the same integer in $\Fp$ and $\F_\Omega$, and primality of $n$ equals irreducibility in the Subject chart; the Subject-realised primes $\Pi_\p$ are the primes to $\q$. A prime is a label on the prime meridian within the horizon.
rows.name: frame_coincidence_below_horizon

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The prime vector: the $\Fp$-valued indicator of the primes in the window, one residue per nonzero residue; the chart weights the prime powers of a deep window by $\log\ell$, the von Mangoldt function; the horizon is a property of the reading, not of the vector.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: Zero-slot: on every shell $Z_\p(k)=\sum_{x\in\Fx{\p}}x^{k}$ vanishes at every nonconstant mode, $1\le k\le\p-2$, and equals $-1$ at the constant mode; it uses no generator and holds on the chart of the Carrier.
rows.name: zero_slot_vanishing

rows.label: B10
rows.predicate: The Subject constants on the shell: $\pi=2\kp$, $2\pi\equiv-1$, $\im=\gen^{-\kp}$, $\im^{2}\equiv-1$, $\E=\gen^{\,\im}$ on the odd lift, $\gen^{\,\pi}\equiv-1$, $\E^{\,\im\pi}\equiv-1$; on $\F_{13}$: $\gen=2$, $\im=5$, $\E=6$, $\pi=6$.
rows.name: subject_constants_shell

blocks.title: The chart: a mode, a mode near every height, a window's spectrum, its count and its bound

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: The chart of a mode: a mode's count is $k=-2^{-1}+\im\gamma_k$ (G4). The chart represents the count of a nonconstant mode by the exponent $-\half+it$, $t$ a free real variable, the height. At a label $n$ that mode is $n^{-1/2+it}$. With a vector's values as labels, the dual becomes their Dirichlet polynomial [chart]. The constant mode keeps the exponent $0$.

rows.label: D13
rows.predicate: The spectrum of a window [chart]: for the labels $1,\dots,\q$ with real weights $\lambda$ of mean $\bar\lambda$, $E(t)=\bigl|\sum_{n\le\q}(\lambda(n)-\bar\lambda)\,n^{\sigma+it}\bigr|$, $\sigma$ and $t$ real. The exhibit takes the prime vector at $\sigma=-\half$, and the deep window the von Mangoldt weight. The five peaks of a window are the five tallest maxima of $E$ on $10\le t\le36$.

rows.label: D14
rows.predicate: The window's primes show the heights [chart]: for every window and weight the mean-removed weights sum to $0$, and $E(-t)=E(t)$. Evaluation [approx]: the five peaks at depth $13$, $39$, $173$ and $1551$ lie within $0.18$, $0.21$, $0.27$ and $0.21$ of the first five heights (A6); at depth $13$ no other of the $4095$ pairs of complementary subsets lies within $0.18$.
rows.name: window_heights

rows.label: D15
rows.predicate: The deep window [chart]: at a label $n$ a mode has the modulus $n^{\sigma}$, and $E(t)\le\sum_{n\le\q}|\lambda(n)-\bar\lambda|\,n^{\sigma}$. Evaluation [approx], von Mangoldt weight, depth $10^{6}$: the ten tallest peaks on $10\le t\le52$ lie within $0.045$ of the first ten heights (A6).
rows.name: deep_window

rows.label: D16
rows.predicate: The count of a window from its dual [chart] (E14): $C_T(x)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-T}^{T}\hat w(t)\,x^{1/2-it}/(\half-it)\,dt$, $\hat w$ the Dirichlet polynomial of the window (D1). Evaluation [approx], depth $39$, heights $35$, $78$, $202$, half-integers: $C_T$ within $0.38$, $0.21$, $0.11$ of $\pi(x)$; Riemann's formula (A6) within $0.48$, $0.22$, $0.15$; the two within $0.14$, $0.10$, $0.10$. At the prime labels each gives $\pi(x)-\half$ within its own bound.

rows.label: D17
rows.predicate: The bound of the count [chart]: for every window, every real vector $w$ on its labels, every position $x>0$ that is no label and every height $T>0$, $|C_T(x)-\sum_{n<x}w(n)|\le B(x)/T$ with $B(x)=\frac1\pi\sum_{n\le\q}|w(n)|\sqrt{x/n}/|\log(x/n)|$ (D16). Evaluation [approx], prime vector, depth $39$, half-integers: $B(x)\le33.14$, so the bound is below one half from the height $67$ on.
rows.name: bound_of_count

rows.label: D18
rows.predicate: A mode near every height [chart]: on every framed shell, for distinct primes $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_m$ of the window with $(\ell_1\cdots\ell_m)^{B}<\p$, $B\ge1$, and every height $t$ (D1), a mode $k$ has $\sum_j|\chi_k(\ell_j)-\ell_j^{\,it}|^{2}\le10m/((B+1)^{2}+1)$ (E13). Evaluation [approx], primes $2$ and $3$, Subject $\F_{1549}$: $B=4$, bound $10/13$; at the heights $0.5,1,\dots,100$ the smallest sum is at most $0.01$.
rows.name: heights_near_modes

rows.label: D19
rows.predicate: The value of a mode at one label: on every framed shell, for a label $\ell\ge2$ and integers $M\ge1$ with $\ell^{M}<\p$ and $V\ge1$ with $MV\ge\p-1$, every nonzero residue is $\ell^{k}\gen^{\,r}$ with a count $k$ (G1) and $r<V$ (E15): $r$ steps of the drive after the mode's value. For the label $3$ on the Subject $\F_{1549}$: largest $M=6$, least $V=258$.
rows.name: steps_after_mode

blocks.title: The dual and the drive: the shell theorem, the parity, the explicit formula

rows.label: E12
rows.predicate: \textbf{The shell theorem.} On every shell, for every vector, in $\Fp$: (i) the dual $\hat v(k)=\sum v(x)x^{k}$ inverts exactly, $v(y)=-\sum\hat v(k)y^{-k}$, the constant mode the mean term; (ii) the Parseval identity (E13); (iii) every mode is an eigenvector of the drive (E15), each nonconstant one with its zero at $k+1$ (G1); (iv) the parity and (v) the explicit formula along the meridian (E14).
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:hp}\newline \pywit{rh}{p20043}{E12}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p20043}{E12}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p20043}{E12} \lean{Rh.chi\_inversion, Rh.chi\_shift, Rh.scale\_shift, FRC.Rh.shift\_power\_character, FRC.Rh.shift\_trace, FRC.Horizon.mode\_expansion, FRC.Horizon.inversion\_res}
rows.name: shell_theorem

rows.label: E13
rows.predicate: The Parseval identity: $\sum_k\hat v(k)\hat v(-k)=-\sum_x v(x)^{2}$ on every shell, the finite Parseval identity of the cycle with the self-pairing $-1$ instead of the complex norm; in the chart of the cycle the $\p-1$ complex characters are an orthogonal basis with $\lVert\chi_j\rVert^{2}=\p-1$ and the same identity becomes $\sum_j|\hat v_{\mathbb C}(j)|^{2}=(\p-1)\sum|v|^{2}$.
rows.name: parseval_identity

rows.label: E14
rows.predicate: The parity and the explicit formula: (iv) $W^{2}=-J$, $F^{2}=J$, $F^{4}=1$; (v) for every vector and every $x\le\p-1$, $\sum_{y\le x}v(y)=-\sum_k\hat v(k)S_k(x)$ with $S_k(x)=\sum_{y\le x}y^{-k}$ and $S_0(x)=x$, along the meridian, from the inversion on the residues with the self-pairing $-1$.
rows.name: parity_explicit_formula

rows.label: E15
rows.predicate: \textbf{The drive theorem.} The drive $(Dv)(x)=v(\gen x)$ permutes the residues and is orthogonal for the pairing of E12 (i); its eigenvectors are the modes $x^{k}$ and their nonzero multiples, eigenvalue $\gen^{k}$, the spectrum $\Fx{\p}$, simple; the modes are isotropic for $k\ne0,\pi$; at $x=\gen^{m}$ the mode $k$ has the value $\gen^{km}$.
rows.name: drive_theorem

rows.label: F7
rows.predicate: \textbf{The closure.} The zeros of a shell are its residues other than $0$ and $1$, and there are no others (G6). ``All the zeros'' of the Carrier is one complete list, the $\Omega-2$ residues of its chart other than $0$ and $1$ (A2, A3). No embedded Subject holds it whole (A4): every reading into its $\p<\Omega-2$ states identifies two zeros.
rows.name: zeros_closure

blocks.title: The count: the generator, the zeros, the critical circle, their order, the Carrier's chart

rows.label: G1
rows.predicate: The modes and their counts: the modes are the powers $x^{k}$ on the nonzero residues, $0\le k\le\p-2$, with $k$ the count and $k=0$ the constant mode. The conjugate of the mode $k\ge1$ is $x^{-k}$, of count $\p-1-k$. The zero of the mode $k\ge1$ is the residue $k+1$. The constant mode stands at $1$.

rows.label: G2
rows.predicate: The count operator: $N$ multiplies the mode of count $k$ by $k$. A count $k\ge1$ and its conjugate add to $-1$. For all vectors $\langle Nv,w\rangle+\langle v,Nw\rangle+\langle v,w\rangle=-c_0d_0$, with $c_0$, $d_0$ the constant parts. So the adjoint of $N$ is $-1-N$ on the vectors with no constant part. Rests on B4, G1.
rows.name: count_operator

rows.label: G3
rows.predicate: The half is forced: $N+c$ is skew on the nonconstant modes exactly when $2c\equiv1$. In a run of $\p-1$ consecutive counts that starts at $m(\p-1)$ or one above, the condition holds exactly for $c=2^{-1}+m$; in every other run it holds for no $c$. Rests on G2.
rows.name: forced_half

rows.label: G4
rows.predicate: The generator and the frequency: $H=-\im\,(N+2^{-1})$, with $\im$ the Subject's quarter-turn. The frequency of the mode $k$ is $\gamma_k=-\im\,(k+2^{-1})$, the eigenvalue of $H$ on that mode.

rows.label: G5
rows.predicate: The generator: $H$ and $\im H=N+2^{-1}$ are skew for the pairing on the vectors with no constant part, $(\gamma_k+\gamma_m)\langle x^{k},x^{m}\rangle=0$ unless both modes are constant, and the conjugate of a nonconstant mode has the frequency $-\gamma_k$. Rests on G2, G3, G4.
rows.name: skew_generator

rows.label: G6
rows.predicate: The zeros: the zero of the nonconstant mode $k$ is $2^{-1}+\im\gamma_k=k+1$. The zeros of the nonconstant modes are the residues other than $0$ and $1$, one each. The conjugate mode has the zero $1-\rho_k$, and $\rho\mapsto1-\rho$ is the one affine map besides the identity that keeps the pair of origin and unit. Rests on B4, G1, G4, G5.
rows.name: zeros_critical_line

rows.label: G7
rows.predicate: The centre: the mode of count $\pi$ is its own conjugate. Its zero is $2^{-1}=2\kp+1=-\pi$, the one fixed point of $\rho\mapsto1-\rho$. Its frequency is $0$, alone among the modes. For a conjugate pair $\rho(1-\rho)=2^{-2}+\gamma^{2}=-k(k+1)$. Rests on G6.
rows.name: centre_of_zeros

rows.label: G8
rows.predicate: The energy of a mode and its conjugate is the smaller of their two counts, $c=\min(k,\p-1-k)$. The mode of count $\pi$ has the energy $\pi$.

rows.label: G9
rows.predicate: The order of the zeros: the pair of energy $\pi-j$ has its zeros at $2^{-1}\pm j$, for $j=0,\dots,\pi-1$. From the centre outward the energy falls by one at each step. Rests on G7, G8.
rows.name: order_of_zeros

rows.label: G10
rows.predicate: The cardinal domains: a mode takes all its values in $\{1,\im,-1,-\im\}$ exactly when its count is $0$, $\kp$, $2\kp$ or $3\kp$. These modes stand at $1$, $3\cdot4^{-1}$, $2^{-1}$ and $4^{-1}$. So the energy latitude $L_{\kp+1}$ is the time latitude $L_1$ one quarter-turn of the count on. Rests on G1.
rows.name: cardinal_domains

rows.label: G11
rows.predicate: The registered domain: a domain of a shell is registered between Subject and Carrier when it is defined from the origin and the unit alone. The positions on the prime meridian and the counts with their zeros are registered. The scales and the phases need the drive and are the Subject's own.

rows.label: G12
rows.predicate: The Carrier's chart, with $\Omega$, $\dS$, $G=2\dS$ for $\p$, $\kp$, $\pi$: the conjugate of a count $1\le k\le\Omega-2$ is $\Omega-1-k$, the centre of the zeros is $2^{-1}=2\dS+1=-G$, and the counts $0$, $\dS$, $2\dS$, $3\dS$ stand at $1$, $3\cdot4^{-1}$, $2^{-1}$, $4^{-1}$. A Subject's nonconstant mode has the same count and zero there. Rests on G2, G6, G10, G11.
rows.name: carrier_chart

rows.label: G13
rows.predicate: The critical circle $\mathcal C$, the points $(a,m)$ of the orbital sphere with $a\,(\gen^{m}+\gen^{-m})=1$: a point and its mirror represent a zero and its conjugate exactly there, with $a^{2}=\rho(1-\rho)$. $\mathcal C$ has one point at each phase $m<\pi$ but $\kp$, and the centre alone on the prime meridian. Its half-turn, the points with $a\,(\gen^{m}+\gen^{-m})=-1$, represents the counts, disjoint from it.
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:circle}\newline \pywit{rh}{p20111}{G13}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p20111}{G13} \lean{FRC.Horizon.circle\_pair, FRC.Horizon.circle\_frequency, FRC.Horizon.circle\_meridians, FRC.Horizon.circle\_point, FRC.Horizon.circle\_count, FRC.Horizon.circle\_counts, FRC.Horizon.circle\_phase, FRC.Horizon.circle\_parallels}
rows.name: critical_circle

rows.label: G14
rows.predicate: The places of the zeros: every zero is $z/(1+z)$ for one $z=\rho/(1-\rho)\ne0,-1$. With $z=\gen^{j}$ the zeros stand on the latitude cycle $C_{\p-1}$, one at each place but $j=\pi$: the centre at $0$, the conjugate at $-j$, the points of the circle at the even places $j=2m$. $2\rho-1=(z-1)/(z+1)$, and $x\mapsto(x-1)/(x+1)$ has the square $x\mapsto-1/x$ and fixes $\pm\im$.
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:circle}\newline \pywit{rh}{p20115}{G14}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p20115}{G14} \lean{FRC.Horizon.circle\_place, FRC.Horizon.circle\_place\_cycle, FRC.Horizon.circle\_place\_even, FRC.Horizon.circle\_quarter\_turn, FRC.Horizon.circle\_place\_phase, FRC.Horizon.circle\_quarter\_closes}
rows.name: zeros_on_latitude_cycle

rows.label: G15
rows.predicate: The Hilbert--P\'olya operator: on every framed shell let $[v,w]=\sum_{x\ne0}v(x)\,w(x^{-1})$. The modes are orthogonal for it, $[x^{k},x^{m}]=-1$ for $k=m$ and $0$ otherwise. So $\gamma_k[x^{k},x^{m}]=\gamma_m[x^{k},x^{m}]$ for every two modes, and the generator is self-adjoint for it on every vector, with the frequencies as its spectrum. Rests on B4, E12, G4.
rows.name: hilbert_polya_operator

rows.label: X1
rows.predicate: The $\half$ of the critical line: the centre of the zeros of a shell is the inverse of $2$, the negative of the half-period: $2^{-1}=-\pi$ on a Subject and $-G$ on the Carrier's chart. Rests on G7, G12; compared with A6.
rows.name: half_of_critical_line

rows.label: X2
rows.predicate: The pole and the functional equation: the constant mode stands at $1$ and is no zero, the shell's form of the pole at $1$. The symmetry $s\mapsto1-s$ is the exchange of a mode with its conjugate, the symmetry of origin and unit. Rests on B4, G6; compared with A6.
rows.name: pole_and_functional_equation

rows.label: X3
rows.predicate: The $\half$ of the dilation generator: the shift that makes the count operator skew on the nonconstant modes is forced, $2c\equiv1$, and the generator is $H=-\im\,(N+2^{-1})$. In the continuum chart it takes the form $-i(x\partial_x+\half)$. Rests on G3, G5; compared with A6.
rows.name: half_of_dilation_generator

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.registered_finite
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — the registered Universe is finite: whatever the totality `U`, what a reading of capacity `R` registers of it embeds in the shell of `R` members. No finiteness of `U` is assumed; the bound is the reading's, a record being finite (29:C1).

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.no_unlimited_supply
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — no reading registers an unlimited supply: among any `R + 1` members of the totality, a reading of capacity `R` gives two the same residue, found by search (the pigeonhole `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`, 5:C2; the idleness of the unbounded supply, 29:C2).

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.agent_bound
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — the agent's bound, the row's instance at capacity `R = records s K` (29:C1): a shell read whole — injectively — into the records of an agent of capacity `K` over `s ≥ 2` symbols has at most `records s K` members, fewer than `s^(K+1)` (`complete_needs_whole` at `o = records s K`, `records_lt`; 5:C2). The row's finitude clauses are `registered_finite` and `no_unlimited_supply` above; the structural cardinality Ω is A7's, consumed.

A3.name: FRC.Foundation.registration_onto
A3.doc: 20:A3, A3 — whatever exists is registered within: the registration of any totality is onto its registered Universe (the definition of `Registered` read back: every residue has a member). The row's "no outside, no host" is A8's and A1's, consumed by reference, not this theorem's: the conjunct holds on a shell read inside a larger host.

A3.name: FRC.Foundation.mutual_registration_count
A3.doc: 20:A3, A3 — two totalities each registered whole within the other have one count: injections both ways between shells force `m = n` (the pigeonhole `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`, 5:C2, both ways). With A6, one count is one Carrier. Silent on a host: a shell with more points registers a shell with fewer.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.observer_part
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, first clause) — a bounded observer is a proper part: an observer with `o < Ω` states holds no injective encoding of the Carrier's `Ω` points, and every reading `ρ` into its states identifies two distinct points (the pigeonhole, `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`; 25:D1, 5:C2). The two points are found by search.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.complete_needs_whole
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, second clause) — a complete reading needs the whole count: a reading of the `Ω` points into `o` records that identifies no two points has `Ω ≤ o` (the contrapositive of `observer_part`). A reader that is not the whole reads incompletely.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.translation_torsor
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, third clause) — the Carrier is a translation torsor (A6): exactly one translation carries each member to each. The origin is frame data: the shell's `0` is the chart's, and the translation carrying `0` to `x` makes `x` an origin as good; the affine frames are a torsor under the frame group (1:C2, `simply_transitive`).

D19.name: FRC.Horizon.label_steps
D19.doc: 20:D19 — the value of a mode at one label. Let `ℓ ≥ 2` be a label with `ℓ^N < p`, and let `p − 1 ≤ N · W`. Then every nonzero residue is `ℓ^k · g^r` with a count `k < p − 1` and `r < W`: the mode of count `k` has the value `ℓ^k` at the label `ℓ`, and the residue is `r` steps of the drive after that value.

E12.name: FRC.Horizon.mode_expansion
E12.doc: 20:E12 (i), Z10 — every vector on the cycle expands in the power modes: at the point `x = g^j`, `v_j = Σ_{k<p−1} c_k x^k`, the constant mode `k = 0` and the nonterminal modes `0 < k < p − 1`.

E12.name: FRC.Horizon.inversion_res
E12.doc: 20:E14, 20:E12 (i) — the inversion on the residues: `w(y) = −Σ_{k<p−1} ŵ(k) y^{−k}` with `y^{−1} = y^{p−2}`, the sign the self-pairing `−1` of the power characters (`geom_sum_unit`).

E13.name: FRC.Horizon.parseval_cycle
E13.doc: 20:E12 (ii), 20:E13 — the Parseval identity on the cycle: `Σ_{k<n} v̂(k) c_k = Σ_{l<n} v_l²` with `c_k = −v̂(−k)` the mode coefficient, that is `Σ_k v̂(k) v̂(−k) = −Σ_l v_l²`: the finite Parseval identity of the cycle, the self-pairing `−1` of the power characters in place of the complex norm.

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.transform_square
E14.doc: 20:E14, 20:E12 (iv) — the transform's square is the parity: `(W²)_{jl} = Σ_k g^{jk} g^{kl}` is `−1` when `j + l ≡ 0` and `0` otherwise, `W² = −J`; with `F = iW` and `i² = −1`, `F² = J` and `F⁴ = 1` (6:B5).

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.geom_sum_unit
E14.doc: 20:E14 — the geometric sum of a nonzero residue over the cycle, the self-pairing of the modes: `Σ_{k<p−1} u^k` is `−1` when `u = 1` and `0` otherwise.

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.inversion_res
E14.doc: 20:E14, 20:E12 (i) — the inversion on the residues: `w(y) = −Σ_{k<p−1} ŵ(k) y^{−k}` with `y^{−1} = y^{p−2}`, the sign the self-pairing `−1` of the power characters (`geom_sum_unit`).

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.explicit_formula_meridian
E14.doc: 20:E14 — the explicit formula along the meridian: for `x ≤ p − 1` the count of `w` over the positions `1, …, x` is the mode sum, `Σ_{y≤x} w(y) = −Σ_{k<p−1} ŵ(k) S_k(x)`, and the constant mode's read is the main term, `S_0(x) = x`.

E14.name: FRC.Horizon.explicit_formula_cycle
E14.doc: 20:E14, 20:E12 (v) — the explicit formula on the cycle: the count of `v` over the first `x` points of the cycle is the mode sum, `Σ_{j<x} v_j = Σ_{k<n} c_k S_k(x)` with `S_k(x) = Σ_{j<x} (g^j)^k` the cumulative read of the mode `k`, and the constant mode's read is the main term, `S_0(x) = x`.

E15.name: FRC.Rh.shift_power_character
E15.doc: 20:E12, 20:E15 — the power characters under the drive, the modes its eigenvectors with eigenvalue `g^k` (20-rh's name; the theorem is `FRC.Horizon.shift_power_character`, LM26; the row 20:E1 that first cited it is retired).

E15.name: FRC.Horizon.drive_orthogonal
E15.doc: 20:E15 (i) — the drive is orthogonal for the pairing `⟨v, w⟩ = Σ_{l<n} v_l w_l` of the cycle: with the vectors read on the phases (`v_l` the value at `g^l`), the drive `x ↦ g x` is `(Dv)_l = v_{l+1}` and its inverse `(D⁻¹w)_l = w_{l−1}`, and `⟨Dv, w⟩ = ⟨v, D⁻¹w⟩`; `n = p − 1`, the indices mod `n`.

E15.name: FRC.Horizon.spectrum_simple
E15.doc: 20:E15 (ii) — the spectrum of the drive is simple: the eigenvalues `g^0, …, g^{n−1}` of the `n` modes are distinct (`pow_inj`, 26:B3); with `shift_power_character` (the modes are eigenvectors, `D x^k = g^k x^k`) the spectrum is the `n = p − 1` nonzero residues, each once.

E15.name: FRC.Horizon.modes_isotropic
E15.doc: 20:E15 (iii) — the modes are isotropic for the pairing: the self-pairing of the mode `k`, `Σ_{l<n} (g^l)^k (g^l)^k = Σ_{l<n} (g^{2k})^l`, vanishes when `g^{2k} ≠ 1` (`mode_square_ne_one`: every mode but `0` and `π`); so the reality of the spectrum is not a consequence of the orthogonality, it is the drive being a scaling by a residue.

E15.name: FRC.Horizon.mode_stride
E15.doc: 20:E15 — at `x = g^m` the mode of count `k` reads `g^{km}`: the latitude `L_1` read at every `k`-th step.

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.closure
F7.doc: 20:F7, the foundation clauses of Theorem closure. (i) The wrap of the height reading: a height `T + p` reads as the residue `T` on the cycle of the shell of cardinality `p`, and the successor reaches every residue of the cycle from `0` within `p` steps (00:A5, `successor_cycle`). (ii) Finitude: a reading of capacity `Ω` embeds the registered heights in the shell of `Ω` members (00:A2, `registered_finite`). (iii) Observation: a reading of `o < Ω` states identifies two residues of the Carrier's cycle, and a reading that identifies none has `Ω ≤ o` (00:A4, `observer_part`, `complete_needs_whole`). No axioms.

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.closure_lab
F7.doc: 20:F7, 20:F2, the laboratory instances: for each laboratory Carrier `Ω = 233, 30089, 2408561` (prime, `≡ 1 mod 4`) the largest admissible Subject `p* = 13, 173, 1549` — a prime `p = 4κ + 1` with `κ > 1` and `p² < Ω`, no admissible Subject between `p*` and `√Ω` (`largestSubject`) — so every embedded Subject's cycle is shorter than the Carrier's and the Carrier's top cell is read from labels up to `√Ω`, beyond every embedded window `√p*`. The largest prime below `√Ω` is not in general a Subject: on `Ω = 401` it is `19`, against the Subject `17`; and `Ω = 13` has no admissible Subject. Primality by trial division to the root (`isPrime_of_bounded`), the bounded quantifiers decided by the kernel.

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.zeros_fill
F7.doc: 20:G6, 20:F7 — the zeros `ρ_k = k + 1`, `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2`, are the residues other than `0` and `1`. No generator.

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.zeros_not_held
F7.doc: 20:F7 (iii) — no embedded Subject holds the Carrier's list of zeros whole: for `2 ≤ p` and `p² < Ω`, every reading of the Carrier's residues into `p` states identifies two zeros `k + 1` and `m + 1` of distinct counts `1 ≤ k < m ≤ Ω − 2`. The Subject has `p < Ω − 2` states, fewer than the zeros.

G2.name: FRC.Horizon.count_conjugate
G2.doc: 20:G2, 20:G12 — the conjugate of a count `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2` is `p − 1 − k`, again in `1, …, p − 2`, and the two counts add to `−1`: `k + (p − 1 − k) + 1 ≡ 0`. No generator.

G2.name: FRC.Horizon.count_adjoint
G2.doc: 20:G2 — the count operator on the nonconstant modes: `⟨N x^k, x^m⟩ + ⟨x^k, N x^m⟩ = −⟨x^k, x^m⟩`, in the form `(k + m + 1)·Σ_{x≠0} x^k·x^m = 0` for `1 ≤ k, m ≤ p − 2`. So the adjoint of `N` is `−1 − N` there.

G2.name: FRC.Horizon.count_adjoint_vector
G2.doc: 20:G2 — the count operator on vectors. With `N` acting on the mode coefficients by `c_k ↦ k·c_k`: `⟨Nv, w⟩ + ⟨v, Nw⟩ + ⟨v, w⟩ = −c_0·d_0`. So `N* = −1 − N` on the vectors with no constant part.

G3.name: FRC.Horizon.half_forced
G3.doc: 20:G3, 20:X3 — the shift is forced: `N + c` is skew on the nonconstant modes exactly when `2c = 1`. No generator.

G3.name: FRC.Horizon.count_run
G3.doc: 20:G3 — the run of counts that starts at `m(p − 1)`: its counts at `k` and at `p − 1 − k` add to `−(2m + 1)`, so the skew shift of the run is `½ + m`. No generator.

G3.name: FRC.Horizon.count_run_only
G3.doc: 20:G3 — the runs without a skew shift. A run of `p − 1` consecutive counts that starts at `m(p − 1) + r` with `2 ≤ r ≤ p − 2` has no shift `c` that makes `N + c` skew on its nonconstant modes: the classes `1` and `p − 2` ask for `2c = 2m + 2`, and the self-conjugate class `2κ` asks for `2c = 2m + 1` or `2m + 3`.

G5.name: FRC.Horizon.generator_skew
G5.doc: 20:G5, 20:X3 — the generator `H = −i(N + ½)` on the modes: `(γ_k + γ_m)·⟨x^k, x^m⟩ = 0` unless both modes are constant. `H` is skew for the pairing, as `N + ½` is.

G5.name: FRC.Horizon.zero_conjugate
G5.doc: 20:G5, 20:G6, 20:X2 — for every `k ≤ p − 1`, `(p − 1 − k) + 1 = 1 − (k + 1)` and `γ_{p−1−k} = −γ_k` as residues; for `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2` these are the zero and the frequency of the conjugate mode.

G6.name: FRC.Horizon.zero_count
G6.doc: 20:G6 — `½ + iγ_k = k + 1` for every count `k`; for `k ≥ 1` this residue is the zero of the mode.

G6.name: FRC.Horizon.zeros_fill
G6.doc: 20:G6, 20:F7 — the zeros `ρ_k = k + 1`, `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2`, are the residues other than `0` and `1`. No generator.

G6.name: FRC.Horizon.zero_conjugate
G6.doc: 20:G5, 20:G6, 20:X2 — for every `k ≤ p − 1`, `(p − 1 − k) + 1 = 1 − (k + 1)` and `γ_{p−1−k} = −γ_k` as residues; for `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2` these are the zero and the frequency of the conjugate mode.

G6.name: FRC.Horizon.origin_unit_symmetry
G6.doc: 20:G6, 20:G7, 20:X2 — the symmetry of origin and unit. An affine map `x ↦ a·x + b` of the shell keeps the pair `{0, 1}` exactly when it is the identity or `x ↦ 1 − x`, and `x ↦ 1 − x` fixes `x` exactly when `2x = 1`. No generator.

G7.name: FRC.Horizon.centre_mode
G7.doc: 20:G7 — the mode of count `π = 2κ` is its own conjugate, its zero is `2⁻¹`, its frequency is `0`, and it is the only count below `p − 1` with the frequency `0`.

G7.name: FRC.Horizon.pair_invariant
G7.doc: 20:G7, 20:G9 — the invariant of a conjugate pair: `ρ(1 − ρ) = ¼ + γ² = −k(k + 1)`, the same for a count and its conjugate.

G7.name: FRC.Horizon.half_unique
G7.doc: 20:G7 — the inverse of `2` is unique: `2x = 1` exactly when `x = 2κ + 1`.

G7.name: FRC.Horizon.origin_unit_symmetry
G7.doc: 20:G6, 20:G7, 20:X2 — the symmetry of origin and unit. An affine map `x ↦ a·x + b` of the shell keeps the pair `{0, 1}` exactly when it is the identity or `x ↦ 1 − x`, and `x ↦ 1 − x` fixes `x` exactly when `2x = 1`. No generator.

G9.name: FRC.Horizon.energy_order
G9.doc: 20:G9 — the order: the counts `2κ − j` and `2κ + j` are conjugate, their zeros are `2⁻¹ − j` and `2⁻¹ + j`, and the smaller of the two is `2κ − j`, the energy of the pair. No generator: the statement takes the cardinality `p = 4κ + 1` alone.

G9.name: FRC.Horizon.pair_invariant
G9.doc: 20:G7, 20:G9 — the invariant of a conjugate pair: `ρ(1 − ρ) = ¼ + γ² = −k(k + 1)`, the same for a count and its conjugate.

G10.name: FRC.Horizon.cardinal_modes
G10.doc: 20:G10 — a mode has all its values in `{1, −1, i, −i}` exactly when its count is `0`, `κ`, `2κ` or `3κ`.

G10.name: FRC.Horizon.cardinal_zeros
G10.doc: 20:G10, 20:G12 — the zeros of the counts `0`, `κ`, `2κ`, `3κ` are `1`, `¾`, `½`, `¼`. No generator: the statement takes the cardinality `p = 4κ + 1` alone, a Subject's or a Carrier's.

G12.name: FRC.Horizon.carrier_centre
G12.doc: 20:G12, 20:X1 — on a shell of cardinality `4S + 1`, with no frame: the centre of the counts is `−½ = 2S`, in the form `2·(2S) + 1 = 0`, and `k + (p − 1 − k)` is twice the centre for every `k ≤ p − 1`; for a count `k ≥ 1` the second term is its conjugate.

G12.name: FRC.Horizon.cardinal_zeros
G12.doc: 20:G10, 20:G12 — the zeros of the counts `0`, `κ`, `2κ`, `3κ` are `1`, `¾`, `½`, `¼`. No generator: the statement takes the cardinality `p = 4κ + 1` alone, a Subject's or a Carrier's.

G12.name: FRC.Horizon.count_conjugate
G12.doc: 20:G2, 20:G12 — the conjugate of a count `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2` is `p − 1 − k`, again in `1, …, p − 2`, and the two counts add to `−1`: `k + (p − 1 − k) + 1 ≡ 0`. No generator.

G12.name: FRC.Horizon.zero_shared
G12.doc: 20:G12 — a zero below `p` is the same integer on every larger shell: the Subject's zero `k + 1` and the zero `k + 1` on a Carrier's chart are one label. At `k = 0` the label is `1`, where the constant mode stands on both. No generator.

G13.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_pair
G13.doc: 20:G13 — on the critical circle a point carries a zero, a residue other than `0` and `1`; its mirror carries the reflection `1 − ρ`, the zero of the conjugate mode; and `a² = ρ(1 − ρ)`.

G13.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_frequency
G13.doc: 20:G13 — the frequency on the circle: a zero and its reflection differ by `2iγ_k`.

G13.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_meridians
G13.doc: 20:G13 — the circle has no point on the momentum meridian, where `u² = −1`, and none at the origin; on the prime meridian, where a point is its own mirror, its one point is the centre `2⁻¹`, of frequency `0`.

G13.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_point
G13.doc: 20:G13 — a zero `ρ` has a point on the circle exactly when `ρ(1 − ρ)` is a square; two points with one zero are `(a, u)` and `(−a, −u)`, one point of the sphere.

G13.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_count
G13.doc: 20:G13 — the count. At the phase `m` with mirror phase `m'`, `m + m' = p − 1`, the circle has a point exactly when `g^{2m} ≠ −1`; among the phases `m < 2κ` that excludes `m = κ` alone; the phase `m + 2κ` gives the same point with the position `−a`; and two points at phases below `2κ` with one zero are at one phase. So the circle has `2κ − 1` points, with `2κ − 1` distinct zeros.

G13.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_counts
G13.doc: 20:G13 — the counts. Negating the position negates both residues of a point of the circle, so they add to `−1`; the point `(−a, −m)` carries `ρ − 1`, the count of the zero that `(a, m)` carries, and its mirror carries `−ρ`; the zero of the count `k` less one is `k`; and on the prime meridian the one point with `x + x = −1` is `π = 2κ`.

G13.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_phase
G13.doc: 20:G13 — one point at each phase: two positions on the critical circle with one phase are equal; and residues `ρ` and `1 − ρ` of a point and its mirror put the point on the circle, the converse of `circle_pair`. No frame is used.

G13.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_parallels
G13.doc: 20:G13 — the sets of constant sum. For `c ≠ 0` the points with the sum `c` are the points of the critical circle with the position multiplied by `c`. Negating the position negates the sum, so the half-turn of the drive exchanges the sums `c` and `−c`. The sum vanishes exactly at the origin and on the momentum meridian, where `u² = −1`. On the prime meridian the sum `c` has the one point `c·2⁻¹`. The sums `1` and `−1` share no point.

G14.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_place
G14.doc: 20:G14 — the places of the zeros. A zero `ρ` is `t/(1 + t)` for exactly one `t`, namely `ρ/(1 − ρ)`, and that `t` is neither `0` nor `−1`; such a `t` gives a zero; and the inverse of `t` gives the reflection `1 − ρ`, the zero of the conjugate mode.

G14.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_place_cycle
G14.doc: 20:G14 — the places on the latitude cycle: `t = g^j` for one `j < p − 1`, and never `j = 2κ`, where `g^j = −1`; the centre is the place `0`.

G14.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_place_even
G14.doc: 20:G14 — the even places. For a zero `ρ = t/(1 + t)`, `t` is a square exactly when `ρ(1 − ρ)` is, that is when `ρ` has a point of the sphere on the circle; and `g^j` is a square exactly when `j` is even.

G14.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_quarter_turn
G14.doc: 20:G14 — the quarter-turn. For a zero `ρ = t/(1 + t)`: `(2ρ − 1)(t + 1) = t − 1`. Two steps of the map `x ↦ (x − 1)/(x + 1)` are `x ↦ −1/x`, and its fixed points are the two roots of `x² = −1` (`circle_quarter_closes` closes the four steps).

G14.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_place_phase
G14.doc: 20:G14 — the phase of an even place: a point of the critical circle with the phase residue `u` carries the zero `u²/(1 + u²)`, the zero at the place of `t = u²`.

G14.name: FRC.Horizon.circle_quarter_closes
G14.doc: 20:G14 — the quarter-turn closes: with `z = −1/x` and `w = −1/z`, `w = x`, so four steps of the map `x ↦ (x − 1)/(x + 1)` return every residue on which they are defined; and two steps move every residue but the roots of `x² = −1`.

G15.name: FRC.Horizon.gram_conj_self
G15.doc: 20:G15 — a mode and its own conjugate: with `k + k' = p − 1`, `⟨x^k, x^k'⟩ = −1`; the conjugate of the mode `x^k` is `x^(−k) = x^k'`.

G15.name: FRC.Horizon.gram_conj_ne
G15.doc: 20:G15 — a mode and the conjugate of another mode: with `m + m' = p − 1` and `k ≠ m`, `⟨x^k, x^m'⟩ = 0`.

G15.name: FRC.Horizon.generator_selfadjoint
G15.doc: 20:G15 — the generator `H = −i(N + ½)` is self-adjoint for the pairing of a vector with the conjugate of another: on the modes, `γ_k·⟨x^k, x^m'⟩ = γ_m·⟨x^k, x^m'⟩` with `x^m'` the conjugate of `x^m`; the modes are orthogonal for it (`gram_conj_self`, `gram_conj_ne`).

X1.name: FRC.Horizon.carrier_centre
X1.doc: 20:G12, 20:X1 — on a shell of cardinality `4S + 1`, with no frame: the centre of the counts is `−½ = 2S`, in the form `2·(2S) + 1 = 0`, and `k + (p − 1 − k)` is twice the centre for every `k ≤ p − 1`; for a count `k ≥ 1` the second term is its conjugate.

X2.name: FRC.Rh.zero_slot
X2.doc: 20:B4, 20:X2 — the zero-slot (20-rh's name; the theorem is `FRC.Horizon.zero_slot`, LM26).

X2.name: FRC.Horizon.zero_conjugate
X2.doc: 20:G5, 20:G6, 20:X2 — for every `k ≤ p − 1`, `(p − 1 − k) + 1 = 1 − (k + 1)` and `γ_{p−1−k} = −γ_k` as residues; for `1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2` these are the zero and the frequency of the conjugate mode.

X2.name: FRC.Horizon.origin_unit_symmetry
X2.doc: 20:G6, 20:G7, 20:X2 — the symmetry of origin and unit. An affine map `x ↦ a·x + b` of the shell keeps the pair `{0, 1}` exactly when it is the identity or `x ↦ 1 − x`, and `x ↦ 1 − x` fixes `x` exactly when `2x = 1`. No generator.

X3.name: FRC.Horizon.half_forced
X3.doc: 20:G3, 20:X3 — the shift is forced: `N + c` is skew on the nonconstant modes exactly when `2c = 1`. No generator.

X3.name: FRC.Horizon.generator_skew
X3.doc: 20:G5, 20:X3 — the generator `H = −i(N + ½)` on the modes: `(γ_k + γ_m)·⟨x^k, x^m⟩ = 0` unless both modes are constant. `H` is skew for the pairing, as `N + ½` is.
